chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, all from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who speaks forgetfully during the prayer, saying, 'Straighten your rows!' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'He should complete his prayer, then he should perform two prostrations.' So I said: 'Are the two prostrations for forgetfulness before or after the salutation?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'After.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for unintentional speech during prayer?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that unintentional speech during prayer does not break the prayer but necessitates *sajdat al-sahw* (prostrations of forgetfulness) performed after the final *taslim*. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the continuity of prayer despite minor verbal errors, distinguishing it from other schools that may view speech as breaking the prayer entirely. The specific placement of these prostrations after the salutation underscores the ritual precision maintained in Imami fiqh regarding compensatory acts.
